cover.title: Docker Complete Handbook
cover.subtitle: From Basics to Advanced
cover.tagline: Package an app with its dependencies once, run it identically anywhere. For developers and DevOps engineers preparing for work or interviews.

items: `docker` CLI is only a ==client==, it runs nothing itself
Sends **REST** calls to `dockerd` via `/var/run/docker.sock`
Daemon owns images, containers, networks, volumes

rows: pid, net, mnt, uts, ipc, user

blocks.note: Same API the docker CLI calls

blocks.title: Mistakes and Interview Points
items: Calling a container a ==lightweight VM==, it is a process
Forgetting containers share the host kernel
Mixing up containerd (manager), runc (creator)
Assuming namespaces alone also cap resources
Q: lightweight VM? Which kernel features? containerd vs runc?
**KEY TAKEAWAY:** a kernel-isolated process started by dockerd, containerd and runc
==Image== = read-only layers + metadata; one image, many containers; stays on disk after rm
==Container== = image + thin writable layer + process (PID 1); template vs running
Unchanged files read from image; modified file ==copied up== to writable layer
`docker rm` **deletes** the layer; persistent data needs a volume

blocks.note: stopped container still holds data until rm

items: Database files in the container layer, expecting a container to outlive its main process
`attach`, then Ctrl+C stops the app
`docker run` again instead of `docker start`

blocks.q: Q1. What happens on docker run, rm, exit?
a_bullets: run: pulls image if missing, makes writable layer, starts main process, streams or detaches
rm loses data: layer lives and dies with container
Container lives only as long as PID 1; it ends, container exits

items: ==FROM== base image; **WORKDIR** folder; **COPY** files in; **RUN** at build time
**ENV** variables; **EXPOSE** documents port; **USER** drops root; **CMD**/**ENTRYPOINT** start the app
ADD when COPY is enough; no USER: app runs as root
Shell form CMD: docker stop waits 10s
Expecting ARG at runtime
Each instruction = one ==layer==; a change **invalidates** all after it
Unchanged layers come from cache: builds take seconds
Stable steps first, volatile last; `npm ci` stays cached; code edits rebuild only the last two layers

blocks.note: Excluded files never reach the daemon

items: Smaller context, faster builds
Stops `.env` leaking via `COPY . .`; host `node_modules` can't overwrite image's
{red:Avoid}: `COPY . .` before installing dependencies
{red:Avoid}: compilers and dev tools in final image; no `.dockerignore` (`.git` gets sent)
{red:Avoid}: separate `RUN apt-get update` and `install`

blocks.title: Shrink Tip
blocks.text: Run `apt-get update && install` in one RUN, then delete `/var/lib/apt/lists/*` in the same layer.

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: How do you shrink an image?
Why combine RUN steps, clean apt caches in one layer?
BuildKit: parallel stages, cache mounts?
KEY: order layers by change rate, build in stages, ship only what runs
==Named volume==: Docker-managed, `/var/lib/docker/volumes`
==Bind mount==: exact **host path** in the container
==tmpfs==: **memory only**, gone on stop
Volumes ==outlive containers==: `docker rm` leaves data
`docker volume create`, `ls`, `prune`; `inspect` shows **Mountpoint**

blocks.note: no slash on the left = volume
stop the database first for consistency

items: `docker rm` leaves an ==anonymous volume==; use `rm -v`
`docker run --rm` also deletes its anonymous volumes
`volume prune` removes unused volumes for **good**
A bind mount hides the image's files at that path

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Persist a database? Named volume on its data dir
Anonymous volume on rm? Orphaned unless `rm -v`
Back up a volume? Tar it from a throwaway container
Each container: own ==network namespace==, IP, loopback; `localhost` is itself
A **driver** links containers and host; same network talks by IP or name, different networks isolated
Default `bridge` (`docker0` switch) has **no** DNS, IPs only; ==user-defined bridge== has built-in DNS names
`-p 8080:80` maps host 8080 to container 80; `-P` publishes every EXPOSEd port randomly
==EXPOSE== is documentation only, publishes **nothing**
`localhost` to reach a **different** container
Expecting `EXPOSE` to open a host port
Container names on the default bridge
`-p 5432` when only the api needs the db

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Bridge vs host: when pick each?
Why no names on default bridge?
What is localhost in a container?
`compose.yml` declares ==services==, networks, volumes; `docker compose up -d` builds and starts the stack
Default network: each **service name** is a hostname; api reaches Postgres at `db:5432`, never `localhost`
`depends_on` alone only ==orders startup==; add a `healthcheck` + `condition: service_healthy`
`env_file` loads a file; `environment` sets keys inline
`profiles: [debug]` starts optional services on request
`compose.override.yml` auto-merges for dev; prod: `-f compose.yml -f compose.prod.yml`

blocks.note: depends_on alone never waits for readiness

items: Trusting `depends_on` to wait for a ready database
Using `localhost` to reach another service
Running `down -v`, wiping the database volume
Expecting Compose to self-heal or scale across hosts

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Why can an app fail even with depends_on?
`down` vs `down -v`: what survives?
Compose not enough: multi-host, rolling updates, self-healing

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Compose wires one host's stack; healthchecks, not depends_on, mean ready.

items: A ==registry== stores images: Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR, GCR; self-host with `registry:2`
Name: `registry/namespace/repo:tag`, e.g. `ghcr.io/iolar/app:1.0`
Tag defaults to latest if omitted

blocks.note: push fails if name lacks the repo
latest is only a default tag name

items: Ship ==semantic version== plus **git SHA** on every build; production pins exact version or `@sha256` digest
`:latest` has no special meaning, never rely on it
Deploying `:latest`: next pull may differ; pinning a mutable tag and assuming it never changes
Pulling anonymously, then hitting Docker Hub rate limits
Pushing without `docker tag`, so the repo name is wrong

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Why is `:latest` dangerous?
Tag vs digest: which is immutable?
Reduce Hub rate limits: mirror, authenticated pulls?
Takeaway: version plus git SHA, pin digests, never trust :latest
**1. Harden:** default ==root== (UID 0), a breakout lands as **host root**
`USER 1000`/`USER node` late, or `--user 1000:1000`; port 8080 (<1024 blocked)
==Minimal base== (alpine, distroless): fewer packages, CVEs
`--cap-add` only what's needed; `--read-only` + `--tmpfs /tmp`
seccomp filters syscalls, AppArmor confines files

blocks.note: ENV token stays in docker history

items: **2. Secrets:** build `docker build --secret id=npmrc,src=.npmrc .`; runtime via files or an orchestrator
Scanners: ==Trivy==, Docker Scout, Grype; fail CI on HIGH/CRITICAL
Signatures: cosign or Docker Content Trust
**3. Mistakes:** `--privileged` exposes all devices, seccomp and AppArmor off
Mounting `docker.sock`: controls daemon, **host root**
`ENV TOKEN=...` or `COPY .env` bakes secrets into layers; `docker history` shows ENV
Deleting a secret in a later RUN: old layer keeps it
`docker logs -f app` streams stdout/stderr live
`docker ps -a` lists stopped and crashed containers
`docker inspect app` shows ==State==, mounts, IP
`docker events` streams die, oom, restart
`docker stats` shows live CPU, memory, network
Reading only logs, never the exit code
Calling 137 a bug without checking OOMKilled
Running `prune -a` on a host with needed images
Using `exec` on a container that keeps dying
Blaming the network before testing DNS inside the container

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: A container keeps restarting: how do you debug it?
What does exit code 137 mean?
How do you find what is eating disk?
Takeaway: exit code, logs, inspect, shell in.
`HEALTHCHECK` marks a container healthy or unhealthy
`--restart unless-stopped`: revives crashes and reboots, not manual stops
`--memory 512m --cpus 1.5` caps one noisy container
`json-file` logs: `max-size` and `max-file` rotation
**One process** per container: scales and restarts alone
==Scheduling==: place containers on hosts with free capacity
==Self-healing==: replace dead containers without a human
Rolling updates and scaling: change versions or replicas live
Service discovery: one stable name; secrets only to needed tasks
No health check: traffic hits a dead container
Deploying `:latest`: nothing to roll back to
State or log files inside the container
No memory limit: one leak starves the host

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Compose vs Swarm vs Kubernetes: when each fits?
How do you deploy with zero downtime?
Why stateless containers that log to stdout?

lines: docker stop web && docker rm web

items: Pin versions or digests, never rely on `:latest`
Use ==multi-stage== builds and a `.dockerignore`
Run as a **non-root** user, no secrets in layers
One process per container, add a `HEALTHCHECK`
